entries.name: An Astrophotographer's Gentle Introduction To Noise

entries.name: Autoguiding
entries.description: An introduction to auto-guiding.

entries.name: Buyer's Guide to ZWO Astronomy Cameras
entries.description: ZWO has a diverse product line. This guide will help you make the right choice.

entries.name: Cable Management Recommendations
entries.description: Some solid advice on cables in an astrophotography setup.

entries.name: Cameras and Lenses
entries.description: Another interactive guide by Bartosz Ciechanowski, this time about cameras and lenses. A must-read for anyone interested in telescopes and photography.

entries.name: Color Spaces
entries.description: Understanding color models, spaces, perception, white point, intensity matches and mismatches (and more!) is crucial for astrophotographers. Bartosz Ciechanowski explains it all in this interactive guide.

entries.name: DeepSkyStacker vs PixInsight
entries.description: A detailed comparison of the pre-processing features.

entries.name: Drift Alignment by Robert Vice (D.A.R.V)
entries.description: Accurate alignment in just a matter of minutes.

entries.name: Flat Fields and Stray Light in Amateur Telescopes
entries.description: A great resource to help one identify and resolve flat-fielding issues.

entries.name: Guide Scope vs. Off-Axis Guider: Which is Better for Astrophotography?
entries.description: Compares the two guiding options in details.

entries.name: Guide to Focal Reducers for Astronomy
entries.description: How focal reducers work, what types are there, and how to use them.

entries.name: Guide to Preprocessing of Raw Data With PixInsight
entries.description: Mistakes that happen during the pre-processing stages cannot be corrected anymore in post-processing. This guide from Bernd Landmann acquaints fellow astrophotographers with PixInsight's tools needed for recognising and avoiding such mistakes.

entries.name: How to Set the Correct Back Focus
entries.description: An easy to follow guide on what back focus is and how to set it.

entries.name: Lights and Shadows
entries.description: This interactive guide to light by Bartosz Ciechanowski, teaches about travel vectors, irradiance, radiance, angles, luminance, and more.

entries.name: Master PixInsight's Astrophotography Statistics: Analyze, Adjust, Enhance
entries.description: Successfully processing astronomical images entails a series of informed decisions. Understanding the data is crucial. This article provides a comprehensive guide to the Statistics process in PixInsight.

entries.name: Mastering Flat Frames: Gain matching
entries.description: This blog series by Willem Jan Drijfhout will take you on a deep dive into the topic of flat frames (Part 2: Flat Panels compared, and Part 3: Bias, Flat-Darks and Conclusions).

entries.name: Optical Glass Types
entries.description: What makes a top-tier telescope? This article will clear up some common misconceptions.

entries.name: Selecting a Guide Scope and Autoguiding Camera for Astrophotography
entries.description: Choosing the right autoguiding equipment can be challenging. This guide will help with making the right decision.

entries.name: Signal, Noise and Histograms
entries.description: Part of Jon Rista's Astrophotography Basics series, this article provides a great bit of theory around signals, noise and histograms.

entries.name: Sky-Watcher AZ-GTI: The Perfect Mount for Mobile Astrophotography
entries.description: The Sky-Watcher AZ-GTI mount was never meant for astrophotography. Oh, the irony!

entries.name: The Differences between CCD and CMOS Sensors
entries.description: One of the best explanations to CCD vs. CMOS camera sensors.

entries.name: The best solution of 55mm back focal length
entries.description: Guidance on how to reach the 55mm back focal length with ASI cameras.

The Astrophotography Manual: A Practical and Scientific Approach to Deep Sky Imaging
A Beginner Guide to Night Photography
entries.description: If you're interested in night photography and particularly deepscapes, this guide hits the spot with it's succinctness.

entries.name: Adam Block's PixInsight video series
entries.description: An extensive collection of video lessons covering both the fundamental and advanced use of PixInsight.

entries.name: Andromeda Galaxy with only a Camera, Lens, & Tripod
entries.description: A comprehensive step-by-step guide. Includes a follow-up videos on post-processing the images in different apps.

entries.name: Astrophotography RGB histogram in nine minutes
entries.description: A lightning explanation of what a histogram is.

entries.name: Capturing Galaxyset
entries.description: A detailed tutorial on how to plan, execute and post-process a deepscape of the Andromeda galaxy aligned with a mountain in Southern Colorado.

entries.name: Chris White's Guide to Fixing Tilt and Spacing
entries.description: Annoying and hard to fix, tilt and spacing can ruin your imaging. This guide will help you eliminate them.

entries.name: Filters for Deep Sky Astrophotography
entries.description: A video series that kicks off with a gentle introduction to filters and closes down comparing the most popular ones.

entries.name: Harry's PixInsight tutorials
entries.description: Newcomer friendly, down-to-earth and comprehensive video tutorials.

entries.name: How to Eliminate Star Halos in PixInsight
entries.description: One of the more challenging issues in astrophotography. Charles Bracken, the author of “The Deep-Sky Imaging Primer”, has you covered.

entries.name: How to Make a Padded Travel Box for Your Telescope
entries.description: Rig assembly on-site can be tedious. A more comfortable alternative is to assemble at home, then upon arrival at the imaging site, install on the mount.

entries.name: Independent Starless Processing
entries.description: This article details a simple and effective method to separate, process, and later reintroduce stars into an image without artifacts. It also discusses how to get more naturally looking stars from a narrowband dataset.

entries.name: Light Vortex Astronomy's PixInsight tutorials
entries.description: An extensive collection of tutorials covering both pre- and post-processing workflows.

entries.name: Orion Nebula (M42) with a DSLR, Start to Finish
entries.description: A complete walk-through. From planning to post-processing.

entries.name: RGB Stars From Narrowband Data
entries.description: Narrowband palettes such as SHO, HOO, etc. produce uncalibrated stars. One way to fix star color is to shoot also in RGB, then blend. In this article, Alberto Ibañez suggests another approach that uses the already acquired narrowband data to achieve the same.

entries.name: Removing Color Artefacts From OSC Images
entries.description: On his blog, Willem Jan Drijfhout explains how to remove color artefacts from images captured with a One-Shot-Color camera.

entries.name: Stacking Multiple Sessions in DSS - The Correct Way
entries.description: Even though it's from year 2012, this video on stacking multiple imaging sessions is still relevant today.

entries.name: Basic Statistics for Astro Imaging
entries.description: Having some understanding of statistics is essential in astrophotography. Here, noted astrophotographer and scientist John Hayes teaches the basics.

entries.name: Beauty and the Beholder
entries.description: On the hidden stories in astro-images and how to tell them. A truly inspirational message from famous astrophotographer Adam Block.

entries.name: Deep Sky Astrophotography With CMOS Cameras by Dr Robin Glover
entries.description: How long should a sub-exposure be? How much to cool? What gain to use? Dr. Robin Glover of SharpCap talks us through the science behind deep sky astrophotography using modern CMOS imaging sensors.

entries.name: Noise and Astrophotography
entries.description: In this presentation, Tim Hutchison from The Astro Imaging Channel talks about the different types of signal and noise that are present in astronomical photos. How noise impacts photography and what we can do against it.

entries.name: APT

entries.description: A simple program that allows the removal of the stars from astrophotography images.

entries.description: Cross-platform and free sky charts.

entries.description: A web application that assists in finding the optimal sub-exposure time. It takes into account the imaging setup, sky glow, etc.

entries.description: A free and open source, self-hosted web application for astrophotography planning. Features both single and multi-user modes, making it suitable for individuals or entire astronomy clubs.

entries.description: A photography planning mobile app (Android & iOS). It helps you plan your photos ahead of time so you’re always at the right place at the right time to capture the best photo possible.

entries.description: A comprehensive web tool that helps astrophotographers plan their sessions using data from Gary Imm's renowned Deep Sky Compendium featuring over 3000 deep sky objects spanning 26 cross-referenced catalogues.

entries.name: SolarHam
entries.description: Real time Space Weather news and solar and geomagnetic activity data from various sources. All in one location for easy navigation. Indispensable for planning solar imaging sessions.

entries.name: Telescopius
entries.description: Free planning and image hosting for astrophotographers.

entries.description: A web-based tool that helps astrophotographers decide between two imaging setups. It quantifies the real light-gathering and sampling trade-offs instead of relying solely on aperture or f-ratio.

entries.name: FocusMax
entries.description: Accurate, automated and repeatable focusing.

entries.name: Modulation Transfer Function and Image Sampling Analyzer
entries.description: This online tool provides insight into the capabilities of a given imaging system. It computes key values such as plate scale, stellar full-width at half-maximum (FWHM), diffraction limit and presents a graph of the system's modulation transfer function (MTF). Very useful for evaluating the performance of a telescope and camera combination.

entries.description: Desktop and command-line FITS workflow for detecting moving and transient objects in aligned astronomical image sequences, aimed at asteroid, comet, satellite, and transient detection.
